title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 69-71). X is smooth projective of dimension n over an algebraically closed field. A_X = Alb(X) and B_X = Pic^0_red(X) = A_X^vee. The previous page proves the degree-1 case of the Lefschetz standard conjecture with Q-coefficients, for the two isomorphisms
- phi_X : H^1(A_X) -> H^1(X), pullback by the Albanese map, and
- psi_X : H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1) -> H^1(B_X), induced by the Poincare divisor on X x B_X.
The inverses are algebraic because the comparison map mu between the abelian varieties is induced by a Q-isogeny B_X -> A_X, which can be inverted in Hom ⊗ Q. The next page computes integral l-adic cohomology: H^1(X,Z_l) = T_l Pic^0, and 0 -> (NS_tors)^vee -> H^{2n-1}(X,Z_l) -> H^1(B_X,Z_l) -> 0.

This page asks whether the same holds INTEGRALLY. A 'cycle entier' is a Z-cycle, not a Q-cycle.

Question 1. Is there an integral correspondence Gamma on A_X x X inducing the inverse of a^* : H^1(A_X,Z) -> H^1(X,Z)?
- By degree count Gamma is a cycle of dimension g = dim A_X: a family of 0-cycles on X parametrized by A_X.
- Grothendieck's sufficient condition: for suitable large n, the generic fibre of the summation map Sym^n X -> A_X has a rational point.
- Then there is a rational section s : A_X ⇢ Sym^n X with alb_n ∘ s = id (up to translation).
- The incidence cycle of s is an integral correspondence. Since alb_n^* on H^1 factors as 'sum of pullbacks' composed with a^*, we get s^*(sum) a^* = (alb_n s)^* = id on H^1. So it gives the integral inverse.

Question 2. Is there an integral 1-cycle on B_X x X inducing the inverse (a section modulo torsion) of psi_X?
- Claim on the page: if Question 1 has a positive answer, it suffices to treat abelian varieties.
- Justification: the Poincare bundle of X is pulled back from that of A_X, so psi_X = psi_{A_X} ∘ a_*.
- a_* on H^{2n-1} is Poincare dual to a^* on H^1, so the transpose of the cycle from Question 1 inverts a_*.
- Hence psi_X^{-1} = Gamma^t ∘ psi_{A_X}^{-1}.

Question 2 for an abelian variety A (with B = A^vee) asks for an integral 1-cycle on A^vee x A whose class gives the inverse of H^{2g-1}(A)(g-1) -> H^1(A^vee). In modern terms this is the algebraicity of the component of c_1(P)^{2g-1}/(2g-1)! (the integral Fourier/Poincare class). For principally polarized A it is the algebraicity of the minimal curve class theta^{g-1}/(g-1)!.

So the page formulates an integral Lefschetz standard conjecture in degree 1 and reduces it to (i) a 0-cycle/rational-section problem for Albanese maps and (ii) the minimal-class problem on abelian varieties.
errors: Not an error but a precision: integrally, H^{2n-1}(X,Z_l)(n-1) -> H^1(B_X,Z_l) has a torsion kernel (dual of NS_tors, as the next page shows). So 'inverse' in Question 2 must mean a section, or inverse modulo torsion.

The sufficient condition in 1) is plausible but not automatic. The natural route through a curve C ⊂ X (Sym^m C -> J(C) is a projective bundle for large m) needs a rational section of J(C) -> A_X. A rational map between abelian varieties is a translate of a homomorphism, so this exists only if J(C) -> A_X splits, which generally fails. Hence the condition must be checked on Sym^n X itself (or with differences of cycles), and the page gives no argument.
In positive characteristic Pic^0 may be non-reduced, so B_X should be read as Pic^0_red. This is harmless for l-adic statements.

ideas.what: Integral (Z-coefficient) version of the degree-1 Lefschetz standard conjecture: integral correspondences inverting H^1(Alb) -> H^1(X) and H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1) -> H^1(Pic^0)
ideas.modern_name: Integral Lefschetz standard conjecture in degree 1 / integral algebraicity of Albanese and Abel-Jacobi inverses
ideas.usually_credited_to: Q-version: Grothendieck 1969 (Standard conjectures), Kleiman 1968, Lieberman. Integral questions on curve classes: Voisin, Colliot-Thelene-Voisin, Benoist-Ottem (2010s)
ideas.where_published: Only the Q-version (degree 1 via Albanese/Picard) is in 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969), as far as I know

ideas.what: Sufficient criterion: the generic fibre of Sym^n X -> Alb(X) has a rational point, giving a family of 0-cycles parametrized by Alb(X) lifting the identity
ideas.modern_name: Rational section of the Albanese map on symmetric powers / universal 0-cycle over the Albanese

ideas.what: Reduction of the integral question for H^{2n-1}(X) -> H^1(Pic^0) to abelian varieties, via psi_X = psi_{Alb} ∘ a_* and the transpose of the Question 1 cycle
ideas.modern_name: Reduction of the integral Hodge/Tate question for 1-cycles inducing Abel-Jacobi inverses to the Albanese
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; similar reductions occur in Voisin and in Beckmann-de Gaay Fortman

ideas.what: The abelian-variety case of Question 2: an integral 1-cycle on A^vee x A inverting H^{2g-1}(A)(g-1) -> H^1(A^vee)
ideas.modern_name: Algebraicity of the integral Fourier/Poincare class c_1(P)^{2g-1}/(2g-1)!, or of the minimal class theta^{g-1}/(g-1)!; integral Hodge conjecture for 1-cycles on abelian varieties
ideas.usually_credited_to: Moonen-Polishchuk (2010, integral Fourier transforms); Beckmann-de Gaay Fortman (2022-23); question raised by Voisin and others

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly asks whether the degree-1 Lefschetz inverses are induced by INTEGRAL cycles. He reduces the general case to (1) a rational-section property of Sym^n X -> Alb(X) and (2) the abelian-variety case. Case (2) is precisely the algebraicity of the integral Poincare/Fourier class (the minimal class theta^{g-1}/(g-1)! in the principally polarized case), a problem only systematically studied 40+ years later.
missed.quote: Y-a-t-il toujours un cycle entier qui donne l'inverse pour H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1) -> H(B_X) ? Si la réponse à 1) est affirmative, il suffirait de connaître la réponse à 2) dans le cas des VA.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows Grothendieck framed the integral Hodge/Tate question for 1-cycles inducing the Abel-Jacobi isomorphism around 1965-71. It also gives a reduction to the minimal-class problem through a 0-cycle condition on the Albanese. Recent work on integral Fourier transforms (Moonen-Polishchuk; Beckmann-de Gaay Fortman) treats abelian varieties, but I am not aware of the general-X reduction via Question 1 being credited or stated this way.

missed.claim: Open-looking question: for which X does the generic fibre of Sym^n X -> Alb(X) acquire a rational point for large n? Equivalently, when is there a family of (possibly virtual) 0-cycles over Alb(X) lifting the identity, so that H^1(X,Z) -> H^1(Alb,Z) has an integrally algebraic inverse?
missed.quote: Il suffirait qu'on sache que pour n convenable ... la fibre générique de Sym^n(X) -> A_X a un point rationnel.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This links integral degree-1 cycle questions to arithmetic of the generic fibre of the Albanese map, and to 'universal 0-cycles'. The route via curves fails when Jacobians do not split, so the answer is non-trivial.

deep.surprise_reason: These are short questions, not results, but well aimed. They anticipate the integral Hodge/Tate problem for 1-cycles and minimal classes on abelian varieties (Moonen-Polishchuk 2010, Beckmann-de Gaay Fortman 2022), together with a reduction from general X to abelian varieties not attributed to Grothendieck. It is not a finished result, so the score stays moderate.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'pour n [-grand-] convenable (donc n vaut[?])' - the parenthesis likely reads '(donc n grand)', with 'grand' struck out earlier in the line.
'Sym^n(X)': the X is overwritten/bold in the manuscript but should be read as Sym^n(X) -> A_X.
'H(A_X) -> H(X)' and 'H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1) -> H(B_X)' refer to the H^1 parts (degree-1 cohomology), as on the previous page.
